newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Europe can't be built on citizens' backs - Jospin.
newsitem.headline: Europe can't be built on citizens' backs - Jospin.

text.p: France remains committed to the construction of Europe -- but not an exclusively monetarist, free-market Europe, newly elected Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin said on Friday.

Speaking to the annual congress of European centre-left parties in the southern Swedish city of Malmo, Jospin said it was an illusion to believe that governments could hunker down behind national barriers to shield themselves from global competition.
But conversely, he said political leaders had a duty to temper market forces to give their citizens the social protection they expected.
"Yes, we are still the vanguard for the construction of a Europe that is united, generous and strong -- but not just any Europe," Jospin said.
Jospin reaffirmed his election pledge to pursue a different direction in Europe with the aim, he said, of putting it back on the rails.
In striving for political integration, Europe's leaders in the past had put economic before social considerations. While growth was strong and jobs were plenty, this worked well.
"But today, with high unemployment, low growth and increasing poverty, Europe can no longer be built on the back of its citizens," Jospin said.
"Market forces, if there is no attempt to control them, will threaten our very idea of civilisation," he said.
Jospin did not dwell on the European Union's planned single currency, saying only in passing that the prospects for it were "delicate".
Welcoming Labour leader Tony Blair's landslide election victory in Britain, Jospin said Europe's centre-left now had a golden opportunity to put employment at the top of the EU's agenda.
The anti-market tone of his speech was in marked contrast to Blair's warm embrace of labour market flexibility.

Jospin acknowledged that there were differences among Europe's left-wing parties but said what they had in common was a lot more important than what kept them apart. Above all, he said, they were all deeply committed to Europe.
